note: SPACE-006 separate platform caches: a compiler cache is bound to the platform that produced it - object files, debug paths, and recorded flags - so a Windows cache staged under a Linux build is either refused or, worse, accepted for a translation unit that was never compiled that way; and a cache written into a source tree is copied by every subsequent snapshot, making a wrong cache a permanent part of the project. src/space/platform_caches.zig routes each entry to the root belonging to the platform that produced it, refuses an entry claiming another platform's root, refuses any path that resolves inside a source root, and refuses roots it does not own, each with its reason. Paths are normalized before routing, so a cache path reaching the source tree through .. is refused rather than trusted; byte counts are reported per platform so a shared cache size is never presented as one platform's. My fixture again needed one more .. component than I first wrote; the implementation was right and the fixture was corrected. Nothing is copied here - the plan is the description and the refusals are the safety property. Fault proof: not enforcing ownership lets the Windows cache land in the Linux root and the placement assertion fails (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
